pages.definition: Empathy is feeling what someone else is feeling. It is not just understanding the situation, but mirroring their emotion to show you are in it together. If they are sad, you show sadness. If they are excited, you show excitement.
visualCues: Mirroring the other person's facial expression
Nodding slowly to show you are following along
toneCues: Matching the speaker's volume (soft for sad, loud for happy)
Using a warm, resonant voice quality
Sighing or gasping in time with the speaker

scenario.context: A friend has dropped their ice cream cone on the ground.
scenario.description: Your friend is visibly upset and crying about the lost dessert.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Exaggerated sadness, loud crying, slow speech, trembling voice.

pages.transcript: Oh no! Look at it! My double-scoop ice cream is all over the dirty sidewalk! I am so sad!

appropriateResponse.description: You should match their level of sadness and disappointment. Do not try to fix it immediately; first, join them in the feeling of loss.
keyElements: Slumping shoulders to mirror their posture

scenario.context: A sibling just opened a birthday present they really wanted.
scenario.description: The speaker is jumping up and down with extreme joy.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Extremely high pitch, fast pace, loud screaming, laughter.

pages.transcript: Yes! Yes! I got the robot dog! I can't believe it! This is the best day of my life!

appropriateResponse.description: You must match their high energy. If you are calm, you will ruin the moment. You need to be loud and happy with them.

scenario.context: A classmate bumped their knee on a desk.
scenario.description: The classmate is wincing and holding their knee in pain.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Sharp intakes of breath, groaning, strained voice indicating pain.

pages.transcript: Owww! Ooh, that really hurts! I hit the corner right on my kneecap! Ouuuch!

appropriateResponse.description: You should physically recoil as if you felt the pain too. Your voice should sound strained and concerned, mirroring their physical discomfort.
keyElements: Wincing face (squinting eyes, baring teeth slightly)
